A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same path-star study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v1's experimental and related-work appendices map to Appendices B and C in v2, which adds a method-relationships appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original seeded training and evaluation experiments on synthetic graphs, including masking, alternative losses, scratchpads, and changes to training graphs and queries.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and Appendix B, including numerical tables and training-accuracy plots.

M1.justification: The masking procedures, BoW/LS/RITF objectives, scratchpads, tree training, query sampling, and length mixing are retained. New Appendix A explains relationships between existing methods without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic path-star task and retain the tree-training, generalized-query, and variable-length/degree scenarios. The new appendix illustrations do not expand empirical dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments, including the shuffling baselines, BoW/LS comparisons, and scratchpad variants. The newly cited Ahn et al. (2025) method is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Model configurations, training budgets, graph-size ranges, decoding procedures, and success/above-baseline thresholds are retained. The nine-layer auxiliary-loss configuration and baseline hyperparameter retuning were already documented in v1 Appendix A; they are not new protocol changes.

E4.justification: The causal-shuffling controls, masking comparisons, scratchpad diagnostics, and graph/query/length analyses are retained. New Appendix A supplies conceptual explanations and illustrations, without adding empirical ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix B newly states an aggregate total of 1,220 reported trials. This is limited run-count disclosure: the five-seeded-trial design, interrupted-run caveat, and variability reporting remain unchanged, with no established increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: The full numerical entries in v1 Tables 6-14 match v2 Tables 1-9. Findings such as only 4/80 successful graph-reconstruction scratchpad trials are retained. The new heatmaps redisplay existing results rather than report performance changes.

T1.justification: The sample-space expression and ranking-loss equations are unchanged. Appendix A adds conceptual mechanism comparisons and worked illustrations, without new formal definitions, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and substantive conclusions retain the claims that decomposition supervision enables decoder-only learning, preventing the Clever Hans Cheat is unnecessary, and scalability remains limited. New Section 1.2 foregrounds the existing argument about the implications for next-token prediction.

C2.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands the mechanism account: it distinguishes shortcut prevention from alleviation, relates future prediction and permuted scratchpads to masking, and proposes within-sample versus across-sample decomposition as a sample-efficiency explanation. Section 5 also removes v1's specific model-depth and vocabulary-size explanations for scaling difficulties.

D1.justification: v2 adds practical resource estimates: a trial can run on a 12GB Titan X and may take about a day, while the complete reported workload comprises 1,220 trials. These are new disclosures, not evidence of changed hardware or training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ahn et al. (2025), Efficient Joint Prediction of Multiple Future Tokens, and makes its positioning against earlier path-star arguments more explicit in Section 1.2. The extensive existing related-work review is largely retained as Appendix C.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 1.2 and a substantial five-subsection explanatory Appendix A, reverses the order of the tree and generalized-query sections, and revises introductory and limitations prose. This materially expands and reorganizes the exposition despite stable methods and experiments.

P2.justification: Five main-text result tables become heatmaps in Figures 3, 4, 6, 9, and 10, and four explanatory figures are added as Figures 12-15. Existing full result tables and empirical plots are preserved but renumbered and relocated.

improvement.justification: The method-comparison appendix, summary heatmaps, and resource disclosure improve clarity and practical documentation while preserving the full results. The gain is limited because empirical support and scaling limitations remain unchanged. New explanatory inconsistencies also temper the benefit: Figure 13a calls leading-node reconstruction 'forward', conflicting with the backward algorithm described in Figure 5b.
